tweets: Calling external contracts risks losing control flow before your function finishes.
A malicious contract can reenter your code mid-execution, causing interactions to behave undesirably.
The primary fix is performing all state changes before making any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern in security reviews.
Alternatively, using a reentrancy lock like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard provides protection.
Always verify that your chosen mitigation aligns with your specific compiler and EVM version.
